prompt.context: Our client is a regional bank that has been growing inorganically. The bank wants to build a new site for all of its app developers. The cities under consideration are Detroit, Chicago, and Orlando.
prompt.question: Recommend a city for our client to build its new app-developer facility. Consider the current economy and employment.

clarifying_info.q: Does the client have offices in any of the cities?
clarifying_info.a: No — this will be the only site in that city.

clarifying_info.q: Do we know the quality of the talent pool in each city?
What is the square footage of the new site, and what kind of construction will be included?
clarifying_info.a: 200,000 sqft; includes a new data center for software/hardware.

clarifying_info.q: Is the bank leasing or buying the building?
How many headcounts does the bank want to employ at the new site, and what are the costs for equipment and supplies per head?
Is the bank planning on providing relocation packages for existing app developers? Is it less expensive to train new employees?
clarifying_info.a: It is cheaper to retain employees; costs are in the exhibit.

clarifying_info.q: What is the culture of the app development team?

exhibits.title: Risks and Impact
exhibits.shows: A table listing five identified risks (Talent, Transportation, Lease vs Buy, Consolidation costs, Not meeting business case) with Impact and Probability ratings for each of the three cities (Detroit, Chicago, Orlando).

exhibits.title: Office Space in Detroit
exhibits.shows: A photo of the candidate office space available in Detroit.

exhibits.title: Office Space in Chicago
exhibits.shows: A photo of the candidate office space available in Chicago.

exhibits.title: Office Space in Orlando
exhibits.shows: A photo of the candidate office space available in Orlando.

framework: Financials for each city: fixed costs (construction/lease, data center); variable costs (headcount, equipment/supplies per head); opportunity costs
Culture and HR: relocation packages for existing app developers; ability to hire new talent locally; lifestyle and commute attractiveness; cultural fit with the creative/open team
Concerns and Risks: feasibility of repurposing the site (exit strategy); talent retention; cultural integration with existing employees

questions.prompt: Walk through Exhibit 1. What key insights can you extract about the risks for each city?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates will first ask clarifying questions about the exhibit (what 'impact' and 'probability' mean, scale definitions) before diving in. Key takeaways: (1) Impact levels are identical across cities for each risk — this tells us how much the client and employees value each risk category. (2) Probability differs by city and indicates how likely each risk is to materialize. High-impact + high-probability pairs are the most dangerous combinations. Detroit has no high-probability risks; its most notable risk is transportation at medium probability. Chicago has all probabilities at the same level or lower than the other two cities, with no high-probability risks. Orlando has three high-probability risk factors (Talent, Transportation, Consolidation costs), making it the riskiest option.

questions.prompt: What does the office space imagery tell you about cultural fit for the app development team?
questions.guidance: The app development team is described as creative and open. Detroit's office photo appears stuffy and traditional, which could stifle that culture. Chicago's office photo conveys a 'hip', modern environment that aligns well with a creative team. Orlando's office does not support the desired culture. This qualitative insight should reinforce or adjust the quantitative risk analysis.

brainstorming.prompt: What additional factors might you consider beyond those in the exhibit when recommending a city?

categories.name: Cost factors
ideas: Higher cost of living in Chicago may translate into higher compensation demands
Detroit's lower cost of living could reduce salary baselines
Construction and real estate costs vary significantly across the three markets

categories.name: Talent pipeline
ideas: Proximity to universities with strong CS/engineering programs
Existing tech ecosystem and employer competition for talent

categories.name: Operational considerations
ideas: Airport connectivity for travel between HQ and the new site
State and local tax incentives for corporate facilities
Quality of public transportation for employee commuting

categories.name: Exit strategy
ideas: Ease of subleasing or repurposing the facility if the project underperforms
Real estate market liquidity in each city
Ability to scale up or down headcount in each local labor market

recommendation: Chicago is the strongest recommendation: it has no high-probability risks across any of the five risk categories, its office space aligns with the creative and open culture of the app development team, and its risk profile is equal to or better than Detroit on every dimension.

Detroit is a viable second choice: it has no high-probability risks and talent risk probability is low (the most critical factor), but the office environment appears stuffy and may not support the team culture.
Orlando should be eliminated: it carries three high-probability risk factors (Talent, Transportation, Consolidation costs), making it the riskiest option with no offsetting advantages.
risks: Chicago has a higher cost of living, which may increase compensation expenses and make talent attraction more competitive
Detroit's office space would require renovation or replacement to support the creative culture, adding cost and complexity
Consolidation costs in any city carry medium impact and medium-to-high probability — relocation and onboarding costs should be budgeted carefully
next_steps: Conduct a detailed financial model comparing total cost of ownership (construction/lease, headcount, equipment, relocation) for Chicago vs Detroit
Assess local talent supply in Chicago (university pipelines, competitor presence) to validate the low talent-risk probability
Evaluate specific office space options in Chicago that match the creative/open culture before committing to a site
Develop an exit/contingency plan for the chosen location in case business requirements change
